audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this a 'Free harass lane' at difficulty 4/10 with Sejuani carry threat 5/10, while the content layer correctly describes a lane Akshan loses from 6 onward. Akshan's win rate here is 22.22%.
audit.why: The content layer, the packet win rate and the already-audited mirror (audits/top/sejuani__akshan.json) all agree: Akshan owns levels 1-3 on Avengerang's 850 range against a 650-range charge, and the lane flips to Sejuani at 6 and stays there. Only the full layer's boilerplate says otherwise.
audit.corrected: tldr, diffRating, carryRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t now read as a hard matchup and say what Akshan actually owns: levels 1-3, then leave.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described as Sejuani interrupting Comeuppance and 'applying Permafrost' behind it.
audit.why: Glacial Prison is 120/105/90s at 1300 range and stuns the first champion hit outright — Riot's text never says it applies Frost stacks, so the Permafrost follow-up is an invented second stun. The real level 6 shift is smaller and worse: the bola reveals stealth, so Going Rogue is not an escape from it. Akshan's own spike is Comeuppance at 100s, missing-health scaled, which is a finisher and cannot burn a tank's pool.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and whys[4] now carry the 1300 range, the 120s cooldown and the stealth reveal, and drop the unsupported Permafrost chain. spikes[3].text carries the same reveal for the late game.

audit.whatIsWrong: Arctic Assault is called '(E)' in three separate strings. Permafrost is E; Arctic Assault is Q.
audit.why: Riot's slots: Q Arctic Assault (650 range, 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, knocks up, and the charge stops after hitting an enemy champion), W Winter's Wrath (600, 9s), E Permafrost (560, 1.5s, needs max Frost stacks), R Glacial Prison (1300, 120s, reveals stealth). The full layer's focus.letters already said Q, so the content layer was the side that was wrong. The decisive interaction nobody had written down: Glacial Prison reveals stealth, so Going Rogue camouflage does not save Akshan from it — and Arctic Assault stops on the first champion it hits, so sidestepping makes it overshoot rather than merely miss.
audit.corrected: Fixed the slot in early, wants.you[2] and wants.foe[0]; added the reveal to spikes[1], spikes[3], whys[4] and breakdown.cooldowns; added the charge-stops-on-first-champion rule to early and report[5].t.

edits.before: Sejuani is the one immobile tank you do NOT get to free-kite. At Level 1 she's slow and you can chip her with Q, but once she has Arctic Assault (E) she dashes in, and every auto and Winter's Wrath (W) stacks Frost on you — at full stacks she shatters Permafrost for a stun, so your range stops mattering. The dash is a skillshot, so sidestep it; throw Q from max distance and never walk up to auto-trade into a shatter. Keep terrain behind you so your Heroic Swing always has an exit. Your one real edge is Level 3: with E up you can swing-poke her before her stun is reliably online.
edits.after: Sejuani is the one immobile tank you do NOT get to free-kite. At Level 1 she's slow and you chip her with Avengerang, but Arctic Assault (Q) is a 650-range charge on 18s, and every auto plus Winter's Wrath (W) stacks Frost on you — at max stacks Permafrost (E) stuns from 560, so your range stops mattering. The charge stops on the first champion it hits, so sidestep and it overshoots. Throw Q from 850 and never auto-trade into a shatter. Keep terrain behind you so Heroic Swing always has an anchor. Your one real edge is Level 3, before her stun is reliable.

notes:
The full layer for this matchup is generic Akshan boilerplate and refers to Sejuani as 'him' and 'his' in at least eight strings (enemyWin, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, breakdown.early, breakdown.wave, tradeGood, tradeBad, report[3].t, report[4].t). It needs a second pass.

Everything I wrote holds either way. This matches the note already recorded in the mirror file audits/top/sejuani__akshan.json.
